symbioteFindings: info signature-changed src/scan.ts#scanFolder: scanFolder changed its signature compatibly; existing users keep working (1 user, 0 untouched · 1 test user)

findings.text: The check that keeps an escaped trailing space only looks at whether the trimmed line ends in `\`. It doesn't check whether that backslash is itself escaped. So `a\\ ` (an escaped backslash followed by a trailing space) becomes the pattern `a\ `, a literal backslash plus a space. Git trims that space and matches `a\`. Also, a lone trailing `\` (`a\`) falls through to line 82 as a literal backslash, where git treats the pattern as invalid and never matches it.

The generated regexes use `.` (in the any-depth prefix `(?:.*/)?` and in the `**` translations at lines 72 and 76) without the `s` flag, so `.` doesn't match `\n`. A file or folder name containing a newline escapes `x/**`, `**/x`, `a/**/b` and every pattern with no `/`. For example, `vendor/**` doesn't ignore `vendor/a\nb.js`, while `[^/]` for `*` and `?` does match newlines. Fix: add the `s` flag.

A UTF-8 BOM isn't stripped, so a `.locignore` saved with one (common from Windows editors) turns its first pattern into `﻿<pattern>`. That pattern then silently never matches, and if the first line is a comment it's no longer recognised as one. Git skips the BOM in ignore files.

Only ENOENT counts as 'no .locignore'. If `<root>/.locignore` is a folder, `readFile` throws EISDIR, and `scanFolder`, and so the `loc` command, crash instead of ignoring nothing, even though a folder of that name is counted like any other folder. Treating EISDIR (and ENOTDIR when `ignoreMatcher` is called directly on a file) the same as ENOENT would match 'when there is none, nothing is ignored'.

Nothing tests the command's half of goal item 2: no test runs `loc` with and without `--no-ignore` to check that it honours `.locignore` by default and counts everything with the flag. Only `scanFolder`'s `ignore` option is covered, in test/scan.test.ts:30.

blind.summary: I found no blocker or major defects. The diff meets the goal. `ignoreMatcher` is exported and handles a missing `.locignore`. It also handles comments, blank lines, trailing spaces, CRLF, `*`, `?`, all three `**` forms, anchoring by a leading or middle `/`, a trailing `/` for folders only, ignoring through parent folders, `!` with the last match winning, and git's rule that a file inside an ignored folder can't be included again. `scanFolder` leaves out ignored files and whole ignored folders unless `ignore: false`, it counts `.locignore` like any other file, and the command passes `--no-ignore` through. I traced every test assertion against the code and they all test what they claim. What's left are minor edge cases and one gap in test coverage.
